newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly lower, with yen leading declines.
"The yen is just out of control," one currency floor trader said after June yen widened losses below support at $0.008647, or 116.00 spot.
Kathy Jones, a currency analyst at Prudential Securities, said dollar/yen could bounce up towards 118.00 spot in the intermediate term.
Jones said the 118.00 level represents fair value if neither the U.S. nor Japan raises interest rates. The 118.00 level corresponds to $0.008507 in June yen.
Floor traders were focused on the performance of cash cross rates. Several traders said they were closely watching mark/yen to determine the direction of June yen and June mark.
Some attributed June marks' gains, which at one point pushed prices above the pivot point to $0.5935, to cash mark's rebound against cash yen.
In addition, other traders were focusing closely on cash mark's performance against Swiss franc and sterling.
They said the mark should continue to rise against the Swiss franc, possibly to 86.00 centimes.

Jones said there were signs that the German economy was improving compared to Switzerland's. Also the Swiss National Bank left the discount rate unchanged at 1.0 percent, a day after saying it was adding more liquidity to the money market.
"The SNB did a successful job in talking the Swiss franc down," Jones said.
June Swiss franc futures tested $0.7150, which at the time corresponded to 1.4020 spot, on extremely light volume.
One floor trader said June's subsequent pullback towards $0.7074, or about 1.4170 spot, was met with heavy volume.
June sterling widened losses, falling through the pivot point of $1.6312, but could rebound if mark/sterling erodes, another floor trader said.
June Mexican peso futures managed to settle higher after staging a light sell-off. After the opening, June pesos set a contract high of $0.126100.
"I'm looking for June pesos to hit $0.128000 and then sell off," a floor analyst said. "If the pattern from January 1996 holds, then the contract should sell off at that level."

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000133 at $0.008654, marks were up $0.0005 at $0.5914, Swiss francs were $0.0020 lower at $0.7099, sterling fell $0.0198 to $1.6226, Canadian dollars were off $0.0027 at $0.7301, Australian dollars were down $0.0096 at $0.7773 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000100 at $0.126000.
